chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Black-Scholes Formula, Step by Step

lessons.title: Pricing a Nifty Call Option Step by Step

children.text: Every piece is now in hand: the formula from Lesson 3.2, and five inputs. Price an illustrative Nifty ATM call, one month to expiry, using hypothetical numbers.
Because spot equals strike, ln(S0/K) = ln(1) = 0, which drops the log-moneyness term entirely and leaves the whole calculation to the drift and volatility terms.

body.caption: The calculation trail for d1 and d2

children.text: Step 2: Convert d1 and d2 into Probabilities

Nobody computes N(x) by hand in practice. A standard normal table, Excel's NORM.S.DIST, or Python's scipy.stats.norm.cdf all give the same answer instantly. For d1 = 0.1631 and d2 = 0.1256, that lookup gives N(d1) ≈ 0.5648 and N(d2) ≈ 0.5500. Both sit just above 50%, which makes sense for an ATM option: Lesson 1.2 already showed uncertainty, and so the probability of finishing in the money, peaks near the ATM strike, and the small tilt above 50% here comes from the positive risk-free drift pulling the risk-neutral distribution slightly upward.
e^(−rT) = e^(−0.065 × 1/12) = e^(−0.005417) ≈ 0.9946. Discounting the strike: K × e^(−rT) = 24,800 × 0.9946 ≈ 24,666.03. Now weight each side by its probability and subtract.

body.label: The finished number
body.context: An illustrative ATM Nifty call, one month to expiry, 13% volatility, 6.5% risk-free rate, priced entirely from the formula, with no forecast of Nifty's direction anywhere in the calculation.

body.title: Where did the ₹440.72 come from?
body.question: This call is exactly at the money, so its intrinsic value (Lesson 1.1) is ₹0. Given the computed price of ₹440.72, what does that tell you about the composition of its premium?
options: The entire ₹440.72 is time value, since intrinsic value is zero here
Roughly half is intrinsic and half is time value
The price cannot really be ₹440.72 if intrinsic value is zero
body.explanation: Intrinsic value for a call is max(S0 − K, 0). With S0 = K = 24,800, that is exactly ₹0. Every rupee of the ₹440.72 the formula produced is time value, the price of one month of uncertainty, exactly the split first introduced in Lesson 1.1 and now produced by a full formula instead of a guess.

body.text: Nothing in this calculation ever asked whether Nifty is going up or down. Five observable-or-estimable inputs, run through one formula, produced one specific number: ₹440.72. That is the entire promise this course opened with, delivered in full.

points: With spot equal to strike, ln(S0/K) drops out entirely, leaving d1 and d2 driven purely by the drift and volatility terms.
d1 = 0.1631 and d2 = 0.1256 in this example, converting via the standard normal distribution to N(d1) ≈ 0.5648 and N(d2) ≈ 0.5500.
e^(−rT) discounts the strike to today's rupees before it gets weighted by N(d2).
Combining S0 N(d1) ≈ ₹14,007.04 and K e^(−rT) N(d2) ≈ ₹13,566.32 gives a call price of ₹440.72.

Since this option is exactly ATM, its ₹0 intrinsic value means the entire ₹440.72 is time value, tying the very first lesson's intrinsic-and-time-value split directly to this chapter's finished formula.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment advice. The spot price, strike, risk-free rate, volatility, and resulting option price are all hypothetical, chosen to demonstrate the calculation, not to represent a live, tradeable quote. Always check the live option chain and use a proper calculator or spreadsheet function for real trading decisions.
